topic: The DNA of Space: From Linear Combinations to Bases
target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school students learning Linear Algebra.

outline.topic: The DNA of Space: From Linear Combinations to Bases
outline.target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school students learning Linear Algebra.

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
sections.content: Briefly revisit vectors as 'movement instructions' rather than just points. Establish the operations of scaling (stretching) and addition (tip-to-tail).
sections.example: Imagine a Robot Scout. Vector v1 is '1 step North' and v2 is '1 step East'. Scaling 2*v1 means taking 2 steps North.

sections.title: Linear Combinations: The Vector Recipe
sections.content: Define a linear combination as the result of scaling vectors and adding them together (a*v + b*w). Visually show the 'tip-to-tail' method on a 2D grid.
sections.example: To reach a hidden treasure at (3, 2), our Robot uses a 'recipe': 3*(1 step East) + 2*(1 step North). This sum is a linear combination of the East and North vectors.

sections.title: Span: The Reachable Map
sections.content: Introduce 'Span' as the set of all possible linear combinations of a group of vectors. Use animation to show a line or plane being 'painted' as scalars vary from negative to positive infinity.
sections.example: If the Robot only has one vector (East), its 'Span' is a single horizontal line. If it has East and North, its 'Span' is the entire 2D flat floor.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
sections.content: Explain linear dependence as 'redundancy.' If one vector can already be reached using the others (it's already in their span), it is dependent. Visually, show a third vector lying exactly on the plane created by two others.
sections.example: Suppose the Robot has three movement vectors: North, East, and North-East. The 'North-East' vector is redundant because the Robot could already reach any point using just North and East. These three are 'Linearly Dependent'.

sections.title: The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit
sections.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that are both linearly independent (no redundancy) and span the entire space (can reach everywhere). It is the 'minimalist' set of instructions for a dimension.
sections.example: For a 2D map, {North, East} is a basis. {North, East, North-East} is not (redundant). {North} is not (cannot reach East). A Basis is like a 'Standard Unit' that defines the grid.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
lecture_lines: Think of vectors as movement instructions, not points.
Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its length.
Adding vectors follows a simple tip-to-tail path.
animations: Display vector v1 (0, 1) in #00FF00 labeled 'North'.
Display vector v2 (1, 0) in #0000FF labeled 'East'.
Scale v1 to 2*v1 (0, 2) in #FFFF00 to show stretching.

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations: The Vector Recipe
lecture_lines: A linear combination scales vectors before adding them.
It's a recipe for reaching any point in space.
Our robot combines three steps east and two north.
This sum reaches the treasure at coordinate three, two.
animations: Create a 2D grid with the origin at center.
Draw vector v (1,0) in #00FF00 and vector w (0,1) in #0000FF.
Extend v to 3v (3,0) and w to 2w (0,2) on the grid.
Move 2w to the tip of 3v using tip-to-tail addition.
Draw the resultant vector (3,2) in #FF00FF labeled 'Linear Combination'.

storyboard.title: Span: The Reachable Map
lecture_lines: Span is the set of all possible vector combinations.
One vector alone spans only a single line.
Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane.
The span shows every location our robot can reach.
animations: Show vector v (1,0) in #00FF00 on the grid.
Draw a horizontal line in #AAAAAA to represent the span of v.
Add vector w (0,1) and shade the entire 2D plane in #444444.

storyboard.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
lecture_lines: Linear dependence occurs when a vector adds no new directions.
If a vector is already in the span, it's redundant.
Three vectors on a flat floor are linearly dependent.
animations: Show vectors v (1,0) in #00FF00 and w (0,1) in #0000FF.
Highlight the 2D plane formed by the span of v and w.
Introduce vector u (1,1) in #FF0000 labeled 'North-East'.
Show u perfectly aligning with the sum of v + w.
Flash u, v, and w to indicate 'Linear Dependence' and redundancy.

storyboard.title: The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit
lecture_lines: A basis is a minimalist toolkit for a space.
It must span the space without any redundant vectors.
North and East form a perfect basis for 2D.
This efficient set defines our entire coordinate system.
animations: Show {North, East} vectors spanning the entire 2D grid.
Label the set as 'Linearly Independent' and 'Spanning 2D'.
Add vector 'North-East' and mark the set as 'Redundant'.
Show only vector 'North' and mark it as 'Insufficient Span'.
Highlight {North, East} in #FFFFFF as the 'Basis' toolkit.
